name: Albuquerque International Balloon Fiesta
unique: Five hundred balloons launch at dawn from a single field, with the Dawn Patrol lighting up like lanterns and a sky that turns into a moving mosaic.
buzz: The 5am alarm is nonnegotiable and worth it; dress in layers and take the park-and-ride. The evening glow is a different show.

name: Chaco Culture
customer: History buffs, photographers, dark sky people
unique: A thousand year old ceremonial city of monumental masonry, aligned to the sun and moon, with roads and signal stations across a hundred miles of desert.
buzz: People call it the American Machu Picchu; the dirt road in is rough and the silence is the point. Stay for the night sky program.

name: White Sands
unique: 275 square miles of gypsum dunes as white as snow, where you can sled down in January and watch the sunset turn them pink and blue.
buzz: Bring a plastic sled and wax; the dunes are otherworldly at golden hour. The missile range occasionally closes the road.

name: Carlsbad Caverns
unique: A 750-foot descent into a limestone chamber the size of a cathedral, with a natural entrance that swallows you and a bat flight out at dusk in summer.
buzz: The self guided Big Room walk is stunning and the ranger tours go deeper; the elevator is unreliable, so be ready to walk.

name: Meow Wolf Santa Fe
unique: The original House of Eternal Return: a Victorian house that opens into a multidimensional narrative maze inside a former bowling alley, built with Game of Thrones money.
buzz: The original is still the best of the Meow Wolf locations; the story is denser and the sense of discovery stronger. Book ahead.

name: Bosque del Apache Crane Festival
unique: Tens of thousands of sandhill cranes and snow geese lift off the Rio Grande wetlands at dawn in a wall of wings and noise, with the Chupadera Mesa behind.
buzz: Dawn at the flight deck is the classic; photographers line up before light. Book the festival workshops early.

name: Taos Pueblo
unique: A thousand year old adobe pueblo still lived in without electricity or running water, with a mission church, hornos and artisans selling from their doors.
buzz: The tour is worth taking and the rules matter, ask before photographing anyone. It is a home, not a set.

name: Acoma Sky City
unique: One of the oldest continuously inhabited places in the country, a mesa top village 367 feet above the desert with adobe houses, a mission church and a view of the lava country.
buzz: The tour is led by Acoma guides and photography requires a permit; visitors say the church and the story of the 1599 massacre stay with them.

name: Bandelier National Monument
unique: Ancestral Puebloan homes carved into soft volcanic tuff, with ladders into cavates and a trail along the canyon wall above a creek.
buzz: The Main Loop and Alcove House are the standard route and the ladders are the fun; the shuttle from White Rock runs in summer.

name: Georgia O'Keeffe Museum
unique: The largest collection of O'Keeffe's work in the world, from the Lake George flowers to the Ghost Ranch bones, in a adobe block a few steps from the plaza.
buzz: The paintings and her studio objects together explain how she saw the landscape; the museum is small and the timed ticket keeps it calm.

name: Ghost Ranch
unique: The red and yellow cliffs where Georgia O'Keeffe painted for decades, now a retreat and education center with trails, a museum and guided tours to her house.
buzz: The landscape is the attraction and the tour to O'Keeffe's house needs booking; the trails are open and the light changes all afternoon.

name: Sandia Peak Tramway
unique: The longest aerial tram in the Americas: 2.7 miles up a sandstone cliff to a 10,378-foot summit with a restaurant and trails in the spruce forest.
buzz: The ride is smooth and the view is enormous; sunset is the best slot. The restaurant is convenient, not a destination.

name: Tinkertown Museum
unique: A maze of rooms built from bottles and cement, filled with thousands of carved wooden figures and animated miniature scenes, on the road up to Sandia Crest.
buzz: People describe it as a fever dream in the best way; the mechanical scenes are charming. Small and unforgettable.

name: El Malpais National Monument
unique: A lava field with ice caves, a sandstone arch and a 17 mile lava tube, on a high plateau where the flows are up to 100,000 years old.
buzz: The lava tube needs a permit and a headlamp and the ice cave is a short walk; the landscape is black and strange and the trails are unmarked in places.

name: Organ Mountains Desert Peaks
unique: A national monument of jagged granite peaks above the Rio Grande valley, with trails into the Organ Mountains and a desert of lava and petroglyphs.
buzz: The Dripping Springs trail is the local hike and the peaks glow at sunset; the desert sections are exposed and the heat is serious in summer.

name: Taos Ski Valley
unique: A steep European style mountain with hike to terrain and chutes, in a high desert valley where the snow is dry and the sun is usually out.
buzz: Experts rate the steeps with anything in Colorado and the base area is small; the drive from Taos is 20 minutes and the altitude is 9,200 feet.

name: Valles Caldera
unique: A 13 mile wide volcanic caldera with grassy valleys and forested rims, where elk herds graze and the Jemez River rises from springs.
buzz: The elk in the valley at dusk are the reason to come and the preserve is quiet; the dirt roads close with snow and the backcountry needs a permit.

name: Bradbury Science Museum
unique: A free museum on the Manhattan Project and the lab that grew from it, with a replica of the first atomic bombs, a supercomputer and a defense gallery.
buzz: The history gallery is frank about the bomb and the science exhibits are hands on; it is the best explanation of Los Alamos anywhere.

name: Canyon Road
unique: A half mile of adobe houses turned into more than 80 galleries, from cowboy painters to contemporary installations, with sculpture courtyards open to the street.
buzz: The Friday night openings in summer are the social event and the side streets have the smaller galleries; most places welcome browsers.

name: Capulin Volcano
unique: A symmetrical cinder cone with a road spiraling to the rim and a trail around the crater, looking out over a field of older volcanoes and three states.
buzz: The drive up is the attraction and the rim trail is a mile; the view from the top on a clear day reaches Colorado and Oklahoma.

name: City of Rocks State Park
unique: A field of volcanic rock columns standing like a city skyline, with campsites tucked between the pillars and a botanical garden of desert plants.
buzz: The camping between the rocks is the experience and the night sky is dark; the park is exposed and hot in summer.

name: El Santuario de Chimayo
unique: A small adobe chapel built around a pit of earth said to heal, visited by hundreds of thousands of pilgrims each year, especially during Holy Week.
buzz: People describe the room of crutches and the quiet; it is an active church and visitors should be respectful, especially during services.

name: Indian Pueblo Cultural Center
unique: A museum owned by the 19 pueblos, with a gallery for each, a courtyard for dances and a restaurant serving pueblo food, on Route 66.
buzz: The dance schedule on weekends is the reason to check ahead; the restaurant's pueblo oven bread and blue corn enchiladas are the local recommendation.

name: Pecos National Historical Park
unique: The ruins of a 17th century mission church beside the remains of a pueblo that traded with the plains, on the route of the Santa Fe Trail.
buzz: The church walls and the reconstructed kiva are the walk and the ranger talks explain the Pueblo Revolt; the park is quiet and free.

name: Three Rivers Petroglyph Site
unique: More than 21,000 petroglyphs on a ridge of basalt boulders, one of the largest rock art sites in the southwest, with a trail through the middle.
buzz: The density is what surprises people and the trail is short; the site is exposed and the nearest town is 20 minutes away.

name: Rio Grande Gorge Bridge
unique: The seventh highest bridge in the country, 650 feet above the Rio Grande, with a walkway on both sides and a view of the gorge that opens under your feet.
buzz: The west side rest area has the vendors and the view; the bridge walk is free and the wind is strong enough to hold you up.

name: Santa Fe Farmers Market
unique: A covered market in the Railyard where northern New Mexico farms sell chile, apples, goat cheese and dried corn, with a breakfast counter inside.
buzz: Locals come at eight for the chile and the breakfast burritos; the Railyard around it has galleries and a cinema for the rest of the morning.

name: Sitting Bull Falls
unique: A 150 foot waterfall in a desert canyon with a pool you can swim in, reached by a 40 mile drive through the Chihuahuan desert.
buzz: The waterfall in the desert is the surprise and the pool is cold; the road is remote and the area can close for flooding.

name: Zuni Pueblo
unique: The largest pueblo in the state, known for inlay jewelry and fetish carving, with a mission church whose murals were painted by Zuni artists in the 1970s.
buzz: The mural church is the highlight and tours are led by tribal members; photography is restricted and the pueblo asks visitors to check in first.

name: Bottomless Lakes State Park
unique: A chain of sinkhole lakes in the desert, formed when groundwater dissolved the limestone, with a swimming beach and a dive training area.
buzz: The water is clear and cold and the diving platforms are the local training spot; the lakes are small and the park is quiet outside summer.

name: Las Vegas Plaza
unique: A plaza ringed by 900 historic buildings from the Santa Fe Trail boom, including a hotel where Doc Holliday and Billy the Kid drank, largely unrestored.
buzz: Architecture people call it the best preserved Victorian town in the southwest and it is nearly empty; some buildings are fragile.

name: Mesilla Plaza
unique: The adobe plaza that was briefly the Confederate capital of Arizona, with the Basilica of San Albino, a double eagle on the wall and a cantina where Billy the Kid was jailed.
buzz: The plaza is small and the history is dense; the restaurants around it serve some of the best New Mexican food in the state.

name: Echo Amphitheater
unique: A natural stone bowl above the road where the echo comes back clearly, with a short trail to the base of the cliff.
buzz: It is a ten minute stop on the drive to Ghost Ranch and people shout into it; the picnic tables and the red rock are the rest.

name: Old Town Albuquerque
unique: The adobe plaza founded in 1706, with the San Felipe de Neri church, a row of shops under portales and a bandstand where mariachi plays on weekends.
buzz: It is touristy and small and the church and the plaza are worth the walk; the rattlesnake museum and the candy shop are the family stops.

name: Oliver Lee Memorial State Park
unique: A ranch house and campground at the mouth of Dog Canyon on the west face of the Sacramento Mountains, with a trail into a cool canyon and desert views.
buzz: The canyon trail is the hike and the campground has shade; it is a quiet base for White Sands 30 minutes away.

name: Red Rock Park
unique: Red sandstone cliffs and a box canyon just outside Gallup, with trails to petroglyphs and an amphitheater that hosts the intertribal ceremonial in August.
buzz: The August ceremonial is the reason to time a visit and the trails are quiet otherwise; the park is a short drive off Interstate 40.

name: Roswell UFO Museum
company: International UFO Museum and Research Center
unique: A former movie theater filled with affidavits, newspaper clippings, dioramas and a very serious research library about the 1947 crash that the government says was a weather balloon.
buzz: It is cheesy and sincere and the gift shop is excellent; the alien-themed town is half the fun.

name: Silver City Historic District
unique: A copper mining town in a canyon with a brick downtown, the Big Ditch that carries the creek under the street and a museum of the mining wars.
buzz: The town is the base for the Gila wilderness and the historic district is a good hour; the university and the bike trail keep it alive.

name: Walatowa Visitor Center
unique: A visitor center at the entrance to Jemez Pueblo with a small museum of pueblo history and access to Red Rock canyon, where the pueblo's story is told by its own people.
buzz: The center is the only way to learn about the pueblo without intruding; photography rules are strict and the red rock formations are the draw.

name: New Mexico Farm and Ranch Museum
unique: A working farm and museum with dairy cows, sheep, a greenhouse and exhibits on how irrigation and cattle changed the desert.
buzz: Children like the animals and adults like the machinery; it is cheap and the demonstrations on weekends are the reason to time a visit.
